title: Stability Partnerships Playbook & SLO Sprint Briefing
content:
Purpose
- Short: Give product, infra, support, release, and dev teams a lightweight playbook for running 6-week SLO improvement sprints and partnered stability experiments.
- Why now: Q1 rollout of new routing logic has surfaced P95 regressions; partnership approach prioritized over top-down mandates.

High-level objectives
1) Reduce P95 token latency on hosted-api by 20% for high-throughput routes within 6 weeks.
2) Improve error budget visibility in product teams (weekly burn reports) so owners can make release decisions.
3) Run 3 low-effort experiments (caching, optimized batching, fallback model) that demonstrate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Who should be involved (roles)
- SRE lead (program owner): Ava Martinez — coordinates sprint, runbooks, retros.
- Product route owners: lane-specific engineers responsible for traffic/canaries.
- Infra/Runtime: Maya Chen — kernel selection, perf tuning, quantization guidance.
- Release eng: Diego Alvarez — rollout windows, feature flags, canary policies.
- Customer Success / Support: Priya Narang — user-facing communications, incident playbook alignment.
- Observability: Samir Bhandari — dashboards, alert tuning, deployment traces.
- Solutions Eng / Field: ad-hoc contributors for customer-specific cases.

Basic cadence (6-week sprint pattern)
- Week 0 (Prep): Align on scope, final metrics, and quick-win backlog. Kickoff meeting 30–45m.
- Weeks 1–4 (Execute): Parallel experiments + deployment runbooks + weekly syncs. Weekly metrics snapshot sent to stakeholders.
- Week 5 (Consolidate): Choose winning config(s), prepare rollout plan, update runbooks and dashboards.
- Week 6 (Deploy & Retro): Controlled rollout (canary -> regional -> global), retro, and next-sprint intake.

Sprint kickoff checklist (quick)
- Confirm target routes (list names + owners).
- Agree success criteria in measurable form (e.g., P95 < 320ms, error rate < 0.3%).
- Reserve rollout windows in calendar (Release Eng input).
- Assign a primary on-call responder for the sprint.
- Create SLO experiment ticket(s) in Jira (template below).

Experiment examples (low friction)
- Prefix KV cache warm-up: pre-populate KV for top 20 routes; measure cold-start reduction.
- Aggressive micro-batching: increase batch window by 10–25ms for non-critical routes and measure latency/cost.
- Fallback model variant: trade slightly lower quality for faster quantized variant during bursts.
- Route split testing: 5% traffic -> new config for 48–72 hours, compare latency & customer-visible signals.

Decision heuristics
- If experiment reduces P95 by >= 12% without >10% cost increase -> promote to canary.
- If error budget burn increases > 2x baseline -> pause and rollback.
- If user-facing errors appear in Support queue within 2h of rollout -> immediate rollback.

Runbook & rollback playbook (short form)
- Pre-deploy: take snapshot of model Version/Config ID, capture current dashboard baseline.
- Deploy canary to single region (5% traffic), observe for 60–120 minutes.
- If key metrics stable: increase to 25% for 3h, then to 100% over a day.
- If any critical alert fires: mute non-essential alerts, page on-call SRE, and rollback within 15 minutes.

Observability and reporting
- Weekly SLO snapshot: include P50/P95/P99, error rate, tail latencies by route, cost per 1k tokens. Sent to product + eng leads.
- Dashboards: master SLO dashboard (SRE-managed) with links to per-route drilldowns (product-managed).
- Alerts: prefer low-signal alerts on change-rate + composite rules (latency spike + error spike).

Communications templates (short)
- Sprint kickoff note (channel): "SLO sprint kickoff for route X. Goal: P95 -> 320ms. Owners: @owner. Weekly updates Fri 10am PT. Link: <confluence>."
- Canary escalation (immediate): "Canary(5%) for route X showed error + latency spike. Rolling back now. See <incident link>."

Training & knowledge transfer
- Short 30m 'how to read SLO dashboards' for product teams in Week 1.
- On-call playbook refresh for Release Eng + Product owners prior to canary.
- Document a 1-pager 'what to do if error budget burns' and pin to the repo.

RACI snapshot
- Responsible: SRE lead (ops execution), Runtime (perf changes), Release Eng (deploy).
- Accountable: Product route owner (decides accept/reject).
- Consulted: Support, Solutions Eng, Observability.
- Informed: GTM for any customer-impacting decisions.

Quick-win experiment backlog (short bullets)
- Add small prefix cache for 3 high-volume prompts. Owner: Runtime. Est: 2 dev-days.
- Tune batching thresholds for 'short-chat' routes. Owner: Runtime. Est: 1 dev-day + 1 canary window.
- Add route-level dynamic fallback policy for overloaded workers. Owner: Release Eng + Runtime. Est: 3 dev-days.

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: experiments cause subtle quality regressions -> Mitigation: pair with small evaluation set / human review.
- Risk: noisy alerts mask real regressions -> Mitigation: refine alert rules and use composite signals.
- Risk: rollout windows collide with high-traffic marketing events -> Mitigation: sync with GTM calendar 2 weeks out.

Metrics of success (end of 6 weeks)
- P95 improvement target met for >= 2 prioritized routes.
- Error budget visibility in product teams (weekly reads) and at least one product-led rollback decision during sprint.
- At least one experiment adopted into default config or codified as 'opt-in'.

Post-sprint artifacts to produce
- Sprint recap (1-page) with numbers, lessons learned, and recommended next steps.
- Updated runbooks and service-playbook entries.
- Changelog note for release engineering and CS.

Open questions / to-do (notes to self)
- Need approval for temporary canary quota increase from capacity team (file JIRA).
- Confirm who owns the customer-facing incident template.
- Get a small eval set from Applied ML for fallback quality validation.

Appendix: Jira ticket template (copy into new ticket)
- Title: "SLO Sprint: [route] - experiment [short name]"
- Components: SRE, Runtime, ReleaseEng, Product
- Acceptance criteria: numeric SLO target, rollback criteria, test plan, canary duration.
- Linked PRs: add runtime and deployment PRs.

---
Notes: keep this doc intentionally lightweight. Use as a pairing guide rather than a rigid program. Add more detail in Confluence if this format is adopted as standard.

End of doc.
